title: Finnish translation: email templates and date/time formatting (backend)
tech: Node/TypeScript backend only -- no new dependency, Luxon (already in use) supports locale-aware formatting natively
keyConstraints: Full replacement to Finnish, no language toggle, no i18n library -- confirmed decision, matches this project's established minimal-dependency convention. Scope: backend/src/services/emailTemplates.ts's 7 templates (confirmed by reading the file: renderRequestReceived, renderConfirmed, renderDeclined, renderCancelledByCustomer, renderCancelledByMasseur, renderMasseurBookingChangeNotice, renderMasseurLoginLink -- covers both customer-facing and masseur-facing emails, all in scope) and backend/src/services/timeFormat.ts's formatLocalTime, which is the single shared date/time formatting function used by BOTH emailQueueService (email bodies) and bookingService (the customer-facing GET /bookings/:id view returned to ManageBooking.tsx) -- confirmed via its own doc comment. Translating this one function means the customer's manage-booking page date display becomes Finnish automatically once this lands, with no frontend change needed for that specific string. Current implementation: DateTime.fromJSDate(date, { zone: 'utc' }).setZone(timezone).toFormat("cccc, LLLL d, yyyy 'at' h:mm a ZZZZ") -- Luxon's cccc (weekday name) and LLLL (month name) tokens render in whatever locale is set on the DateTime object (defaults to en-US if never set, which is why it's English today); add .setLocale('fi') to the chain. The format PATTERN itself should also switch to Finnish convention, not just the locale of the day/month name tokens -- Finnish convention is 24-hour time (not AM/PM) and day-first date order; a natural Finnish rendering would be closer to 'keskiviikko 12. elokuuta 2026 klo 9.00' (weekday, day. month-in-genitive year, klo = 'at') than a literal token-for-token port of the English pattern. Get the exact Luxon format string and Finnish grammar right (e.g. Finnish month names in a date context take the genitive/partitive form depending on construction -- 'elokuuta' not 'Elokuu' when following a day number) -- Ville (the user) is a native Finnish speaker and should review the actual rendered output during testing for naturalness, not just correctness of the mechanism. Email subject lines (all 7 templates) must also be translated, including the sanitizeForSubject() header-injection guard (backend/src/services/emailTemplates.ts line 16) -- do not weaken or remove that guard while changing the surrounding text.
description: Translate all customer- and masseur-facing email copy (subject + body, all 7 templates) to natural Finnish, and switch the shared date/time formatting function (formatLocalTime) to Finnish locale and convention (24-hour time, day-first date order, natural Finnish weekday/month grammar). This is a full replacement -- no English fallback, no language toggle.
acceptanceCriteria: All 7 email templates (renderRequestReceived, renderConfirmed, renderDeclined, renderCancelledByCustomer, renderCancelledByMasseur, renderMasseurBookingChangeNotice, renderMasseurLoginLink) have Finnish subject lines and body text
formatLocalTime renders dates in Finnish (weekday and month names via .setLocale('fi')) using Finnish date/time convention (24-hour time, day-first order), not a literal port of the English pattern
sanitizeForSubject()'s header-injection guard is preserved and still applied to the same fields it currently protects

Existing tests referencing specific English strings (emailTemplates.test.ts, emailWorker.test.ts, and any integration test asserting on formatLocalTime's exact output) are deliberately updated to the new Finnish text/format, with the update reasoned through, not just patched to make failures go away
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in backend/ (frontend should be unaffected since no frontend files change)
relevantFilePaths: backend/test/unit/emailWorker.test.ts (if it asserts on rendered email text)
securityConsiderations: None new -- sanitizeForSubject's existing header-injection protection must remain intact and applied to the same interpolated values, just with translated surrounding text.
